title: Paired errors gave no clear joint lake-level probability gain at 1970-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether paired forecast errors improve the probability that Superior and Michigan-Huron will both exceed their past seasonal means six months later. We used coordinated v2025 monthly levels and 660 origins in 1970-2024. Each annual fit and error pool used only earlier completed targets. The paired rule and the independent rule had the same marginal probabilities. Pairing reduced mean Brier loss from 0.125550 to 0.123703, a 1.47% reduction. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -0.80% to 4.04%. Other block lengths, a low-water event, upper-quartile thresholds and a twenty-year error pool also had intervals across zero. Pooled error correlations were positive, but they did not establish a clear joint probability gain. This is a null benchmark for one method, not evidence that the lakes are independent. Revised data, overlapping targets, pooled seasonal errors and 55 test years limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, every probability and score, resampling evidence, internal audits and a static figure are included. External raw data stay outside the package.

display.caption: Primary joint-event Brier loss and descriptive calibration for six-month forecasts at 660 origins in 1970-2024. Paired errors gave a 1.47% point reduction in loss, with conditional 95% five-year block limits of -0.80% to 4.04%. Calibration bins contain dependent months and have no uncertainty bars.
